get.description: Reported first, then newest — the order the A6 screen reads in.

post.description: Withhold a comment from everyone but its author and the administrators.
Leave the comment standing and take it off the queue.

get.description: Show both measured and unknown inputs so estimate confidence is explainable.
Your shelves by default; `shared=true` adds the ones others opened up.

put.description: Idempotent: adding a title already on the shelf changes nothing.

patch.description:
Only the author edits. An administrator can hide or delete, never rewrite.

Putting words in someone's mouth is a different power from moderation, and
the audit trail would not show it.

put.description: Idempotent: a double-tap must not become a second like.

post.description:
202, and never a count: the reporter learns nothing about other reports.

Reporting twice updates the reason rather than stacking, so a single reader
cannot make a remark look widely objected to.

get.description:
Hidden comments stay visible to their author and to administrators.

Silently vanishing a remark teaches the author nothing; the state is part of
the response so the client can mark it as withheld.

post.description:
Append a marker by hand, after the ones detection produced.

Ordinals are positions in the index, not identifiers, so a manual marker
takes the next one rather than being inserted in time order — renumbering
every later marker would invalidate the ids clips point at.

delete.description: Clips cut from this marker keep working; their `marker_id` becomes null.
Idempotent: withdrawing a rating you never gave is not an error.

put.description: Set-or-replace, so re-rating from a second tab cannot collide.

get.description:
Titles like this one.

Scoped the same way the library is: a neighbour you are not allowed to see
in the grid must not appear here either, or the related row becomes a way
to enumerate someone else's private titles.
Serve the generated contact sheet only for an existing active item.

post.description: Queue a fresh search for one monitor without waiting for its daily slot.

get.description:
What "Playing on" reads: this account's live transcodes.

Direct play deliberately does not appear. A direct-playing client streams
the file without asking the server to keep any session state, so there is
nothing here to report — the absence of a row for a device *is* the signal
that it is not transcoding, and inventing a record would mean tracking
playback the server otherwise has no reason to know about.
List queue jobs with deterministic sorting and current priority-based ETAs.

delete.description: Remove the user's signals so the next refresh starts from an empty profile.

post.description: Hand a title to someone with a note. They are told who sent it.

get.description:
The one place in the product where another person is named.

Everything else is anonymous under `anonymous_social`; a hand-picked
recommendation is worthless without knowing whose taste it was.

post.description: Revalidate one cached release and submit it exactly once.
Queue a user's external fan-out without delaying the local search response.

get.description: Read one user's progressive indexer search with stable, shared filters.

Counts for the filter sidebar, from the same pipeline as the results.

Everything the list does to a row — the visibility scope, the content filter
rules — happens here too. A count the list cannot deliver is worse than no
count, because a reader will click it.
Your outbox without read receipts: `seen_at` is blanked for the sender.

delete.description: Either party can remove it: the recipient dismisses, the sender withdraws.

get.description:
Trending is recent watching, not all-time rating.

A clip cut yesterday that everyone opened should lead over one from March
with a slightly better average, so trending counts progress events on the
parent title within the window rather than sorting by score.

post.description:
Cut clips at the detected scene boundaries of a title.

One clip per marker, in order, skipping any that would overlap a clip that
already exists — so this never disturbs a cut placed by hand, and never
re-cuts a marker it has already covered.

`maximum` bounds one call rather than the title: calling again picks up at
the first uncovered marker, so a long film can be worked through a few
clips at a time instead of producing a hundred in one press.

A marker is a boundary, not a length: the clip runs from the boundary for
the requested duration or to the end of the scene, whichever is shorter, so
a five-second shot does not become a minute of the following one.
Idempotent: adding something already queued is not an error.
